messages:
ops-bot: Pager alert: 60% increase in 5xx from hosted inference API in us-east-1 beginning ~08:03 UTC, p95 latency up 2.2s. @oncall alex
alex: pulling logs now, thanks. any customer escalations yet?
support-bot: 4 customers opened high-severity chats citing timeouts and 503s, first ticket at 08:05 UTC — ticket IDs: #2134, #2137, #2141
sara: I can repro a burst locally hitting /v1/generate with a sustained 100rps and see intermittent 502/503 at the edge gateway. stack traces show upstream read timeout from inference-proxy clusters.
ben: checking autoscale and pool sizes — saw an autoscaler cooldown triggered at 08:02, target replicas stayed at 4 while CPU spiked to 95%.
mike: metric note: inference-batcher queue length jumped and kv-cache hit-rate dropped 20% around the same time. suspect cache warmup + large concurrent prefixes.
alex: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) widen concurrency soft-limit on dedicated nodes 2) enable fallback to smaller model variant 3) add temporary routing to eu-west for affected customers. thoughts?
sara: routing customers will change latency but will relieve us. can we push quick route policy for clients tagged as non-compliant with region?
ben: I can bump replica target from 4 -> 8 for inference-proxy in us-east; doing a quick scale now. running:
```
kubectl scale deployment/inference-proxy -n hosted --replicas=8
```
ops-bot: Scale command accepted; rollout starting (8 -> 8 ready 0/8 -> 8/8). expected ready in ~45s
ria: while that rolls, I'm going to temporarily increase the upstream timeout between gateway and proxy from 2s -> 6s to avoid immediate 502s. doing patch to nginx config in staging then production.
alex: good. also patch circuit-breaker to lower failure threshold so we fail faster to variant instead of cascading 5xx. ben, can you check if cache nodes are saturated?
ben: cache pods show OOM spikes on a few hosts; restarting one showed hit-rate recovery. suspect we hit large KV eviction due to a customer burst with big prompt prefixes. logs attached: `OOMKilled at 08:04 inferred by memory spike`
mike: action: add temporary prefix-KV TTL to 60s for large keys to avoid thrash. I'll push config change to kv-cache service.
support-bot: customer #2134 reports improvement after ~2:20, still seeing occasional timeouts. said they saw 503 -> 200 for subsequent calls.
sara: rollout finishing: inference-proxy now 8/8 ready. nginx timeout increased in prod. preliminary 5xx rate dropped ~70% over last 2 mins per dashboard (link: https://dash.redwood/alerts/6087654321)
alex: nice. capture repro steps for postmortem: 1) seed a 100rps sustained with variable prompt lengths, 2) single customer with many long-prefix requests to kv-cache, 3) autoscaler cooldown prevented scale out. assign action items.
ben: postmortem owners: ben -> autoscaler tuning, ria -> nginx timeout policy + circuit-breaker defaults, mike -> kv-cache eviction/TTL guardrails, sara -> runbook updates for fallback routing and canarying route changes.
alex: timeline note for postmortem doc: incident start 08:03 UTC, peak 08:04-08:06, mitigations applied 08:05-08:07, gradual recovery 08:07-08:12.
ria: I'll follow up with a patch to set a hard limit on largest KV key size and add eviction metrics.
mike: I'll add a safeguard that rejects requests with prefix > 200k chars with 4xx rather than letting cache blow memory.
sara: also recommend changing autoscaler cooldown rules: allow one aggressive scale-per-minute for sudden CPU spikes from inference jobs.
alex: communication: send an initial incident summary to affected customers + post a status update on status.redwood.com. support-bot, can you draft?
support-bot: Drafted: "We experienced elevated 5xx/timeouts in us-east-1 between 08:03-08:12 UTC due to a cache eviction and autoscaling lag during a customer traffic burst. Mitigations included scaling proxy pool, increasing upstream timeouts, and applying temporary cache TTLs. We are investigating long-term fixes." Shall I send?
alex: yes, send and include timeline and next steps. we will SOC-review the postmortem tomorrow.
ben: immediate follow-ups created in tasks: INF-AUTO-71, KV-THRASH-12, NGX-CB-9. I'll own INF-AUTO-71.
ria: adding monitoring alerts: kv-cache memory pressure alert to P2 threshold and autoscaler lag metric to P1.
sara: runbook update: adding a short playbook for prefix-thrash events and a checklist for routing to alternate regions. I'll PR after SOC review.
alex: thanks all. good containment. we'll reconvene for postmortem doc at 14:00 UTC. closing war room thread. :white_check_mark:
